answer: Staked peer review with spot checks bills the attacker before it pays anyone. Every reviewer posts a bond, a tenth of submissions get a second unrelated auditor, and duplicates are caught by replay rather than by name. One thousand renamed copies of one answer pass a name check and fail the first re-run, costing the reviewer the bond. A grove of look-alikes sends one ripple through the reviewer pool and every holder feels it. A single wharf address cannot hide that.
